title: Space-query exponent curve of 3SUM indexing
formal:
Determine the query-exponent curve \(\tau_{\mathrm{3SI}}:[1,2]\to\mathbb R\) to absolute accuracy \(1/100\) at every point, where
\[
\tau_{\mathrm{3SI}}(s)=\inf\{t\ge0:\ \forall\eta\in\mathbb Q_{>0}\ \exists(P,Q)\text{ satisfying }S(n)=O(n^{s+\eta}),\ T(n)=O(n^{t+\eta})\}.
\]
Here \((P,Q)\) is a uniform randomized static index for the two-set sum-membership problem below. Space and query time obey their bounds on every random outcome, while each fixed input/query is correct with probability at least \(2/3\). Preprocessing time is unrestricted.
definitions:
For each integer \(n\ge2\), the input consists of two explicit arrays listing sets \(A,B\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n^4-1\}\), each of cardinality \(n\). There are no repetitions within a set; the two sets may intersect, and their array order is arbitrary. A query supplies \(z\in\{0,\ldots,2n^4-2\}\) and asks for the Boolean value of \(z\in A+B\), where \(A+B=\{a+b:a\in A,b\in B\}\) uses ordinary integer addition. No pair of witnesses is required.

Fix the word length to \(w=10\lceil\log_2(n+2)\rceil\) bits. This fixed ten resolves the former text’s contradictory generic algorithm-chosen word constant. A uniform sequential word RAM has one finite program, word registers and word-addressed cells. Unit-cost instructions are copying, addressed reads and writes, comparison, branching, Boolean bit operations, logical shifts, addition, subtraction and multiplication modulo \(2^w\), and integer quotient and remainder with nonzero divisor. A shift by at least \(w\) returns zero. Multiword work pays for each constituent instruction. It may generate independent uniform random words. All addresses fit in one word. There is no advice, uncharged lookup table, input-dependent oracle or access to arbitrarily long integers in one step.

The preprocessor \(P\) receives \(n,A,B\) and terminates almost surely with a static representation. Its time and temporary workspace are unrestricted within the RAM's address model; the index retained for queries must obey the space bound on every outcome. Every retained input copy, random seed, hash parameter, table and other input-dependent datum counts in that space. The query program \(Q\) receives \(n,z\), read-only access to the index and fresh private random words. Each call starts without other input-dependent state and returns a bit within the worst-case query bound on every random tape. Temporary query work is charged instruction by instruction; no input-dependent information can be carried between calls outside the counted index. The original arrays are available only if stored in that index.

For every fixed \(n,A,B,z\), correctness probability at least \(2/3\) averages both preprocessing randomness and that call's independent randomness. This is not a simultaneous all-query success requirement for each sampled index, nor a guarantee for queries chosen adaptively after inspecting its randomness. For each chosen \(s,t,\eta\), one pair of finite programs and constants handles all sizes and inputs; the constants in both big-O bounds may depend on those three fixed parameters. Bounds mean that such constants and a size threshold work for every sufficiently large \(n\); finitely many smaller sizes must still be handled correctly. The parameters select programs and are not real-number machine inputs.

The two sorted input sets give linear-space, linear-query scanning, so the defining set is nonempty and \(0\le\tau_{\mathrm{3SI}}(s)\le1\). At \(s=2\), storing the sorted sumset and binary-searching it gives \(\tau_{\mathrm{3SI}}(2)=0\). The curve is nonincreasing in \(s\). Infima need not be attained. The all-positive-rational \(\eta\) convention absorbs subpolynomial factors but does not identify a zero query exponent with a polylogarithmic query algorithm. A different finite program may be selected for each \(\eta\), as in the saved user-approved curve.
why: The curve asks how much information about a quadratic family of sums must be stored to support reusable membership queries, a general representation barrier underlying several string indexes.

context_blocks.text: Storing all sums and storing only the two sets give different endpoints of a reusable-query tradeoff. The curve asks for the intrinsic frontier between those representations.

The strongest historical conjecture forbidding all simultaneous subquadratic-space and sublinear-query improvements was refuted by later algorithms, as the 2026 introduction explicitly records. It must not be used as an established lower bound.

The 2026 paper gives a uniform RAM tradeoff \(ST=\widetilde O(n^{5/2})\), improving its previous frontier for \(n^{3/2}\ll S\ll n^{7/4}\). Its one-array witness version and the two-set decision formulation must be distinguished when transferring statements. The reported improvement does not supply a matching curve.

progress.text: The source defines the two-array decision problem and distinguishes polylogarithmic-query and stronger sublinear-query hardness conjectures.

The revised paper records the refutation of the stronger conjecture and improves intermediate upper bounds, including a uniform RAM implementation. Its survey still identifies static-data-structure lower bounds as a major obstacle.

answer_criterion: Give an explicit unambiguous function \(g:[1,2]\to\mathbb R\) and a complete mathematically correct Lean-checked proof that \(|g(s)-\tau_{\mathrm{3SI}}(s)|\le1/100\) for every real \(s\in[1,2]\). Uniform certified bounding functions of gap at most \(1/50\) suffice through their midpoint. Exact equality also qualifies. The defining infimum renamed as \(g\), a plot, finitely many checked points, or an upper bound alone is insufficient. No hardness conjecture is assumed; conditional lower bounds establish only conditional conclusions. An exponent-zero endpoint or its numerical approximation does not establish the older polylogarithmic-query threshold question.
status_note: The saved user-approved curve is a precise editorial quantitative target. The checked 2026 primary paper improves upper tradeoffs and explicitly records failure of the strongest old conjecture; it does not characterize this full curve to accuracy 1/100. Bounded checks through 18 September 2026 found no verified resolution, without exhaustive certification.

previous.title: Subquadratic-space 3SUM indexing with polylogarithmic queries
previous.formal: Do there exist constants \(\delta>0\) and \(C\ge1\) and uniform randomized preprocessing and query algorithms such that, for every \(n\ge2\) and \(A,B\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n^4-1\}\) with \(|A|=|B|=n\), the resulting static index uses at most \(O(n^{2-\delta})\) words and answers whether \(z\in A+B\) in \(O((\log n)^C)\) worst-case time? Each fixed query must be correct with probability at least \(2/3\).
previous.definitions: A uniform sequential word RAM has a fixed finite program, word-sized registers and addressed memory cells. Unit-cost instructions are reads and writes, comparisons, branching, addition, subtraction, multiplication, integer division with nonzero divisor, Boolean bit operations and logical shifts. Arithmetic stored in one word is modulo \(2^w\); shifts by at least \(w\) yield zero. Addresses must fit the available word size. All table construction and input-dependent auxiliary memory count; there is no free advice or input-dependent oracle. Randomized programs may generate independent uniform random words. Use \(w=\lceil10\log_2(n+2)\rceil\)-bit words. A query is \(z\in\{0,\ldots,2n^4-2\}\), and \(A+B=\{a+b:a\in A,b\in B\}\) uses ordinary integer addition without wraparound. Preprocessing time is unrestricted but must terminate almost surely; its resulting representation must always respect the space budget. Randomized queries use fresh internal randomness, and the per-query success probability is over both preprocessing and query randomness for every fixed \((A,B,z)\). Queries read a static representation and cannot carry free input-dependent information across calls. All stored inputs, hash seeds and auxiliary tables count toward space. The constants and programs must be independent of the input and \(n\). A polynomial universe with exponent four avoids the small-universe direct-address case; it is an explicit benchmark regime of the broader indexing question.
previous.answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof of the stated existence claim or its logical negation, with the same inputs, computation model, space allowance, quantifiers and cost guarantees. A result for a restricted input family or a different model does not decide the full target.
